description: Read the full conversation. Use any earlier `step` fields as confirmed and exhausted steps. Check whether the last message, which is always from the agent, starts the next valid declared workflow step. If yes, return that step id. If not, return `in-between-step`. In all non-error cases, return one to three short user replies for the next turn. Replies must always be written as user messages, never as agent messages. The workflow is sequential and ends only when the agent delivers its final closing message.
goals: Detect whether the latest auditor agent message starts the next valid declared workflow step.
Return `in-between-step` when the latest agent message does not start a new declared workflow step.
Return one to three short user replies that advance the conversation toward the next declared step.
Declared workflow steps are sequential and cannot be skipped.

step_consumption: Declared workflow steps are sequential and cannot be skipped.

A declared workflow step that already appears as a `step` field on any earlier agent message is fully consumed and exhausted. It must never be returned again for any later agent message, even if the later message appears related to the same topic or uses similar vocabulary.
If you are tempted to return a step that already exists in the conversation history, stop and return `in-between-step` instead.
Any returned step must refer only to the latest agent message.
Return a declared workflow step only if the latest agent message clearly and unambiguously starts that new declared step.
in_between_step_usage: `in-between-step` is the correct return value when the latest agent message continues the flow but does not clearly start a new declared step.
This includes follow-up questions, clarifications, or intermediate responses that do not start a new declared workflow step.
Always return one to three valid user replies even when returning `in-between-step`.
reply_generation: Each reply must be written in first person from the user's point of view.
Never write replies from the agent's point of view.
Do not generate assistant-style or explanatory replies.

The conversation array will include an initial system message containing metadata: payment_id, transaction_id, intent_mandate_id, cart_mandate_id, and payment_mandate_id. Extract and use these exact values when replies require identifiers.

steps.description: Step 1 of 5. Always return this step for the first agent message in the conversation: the one responding to the fixed opening user message, 'Hi, I'm not happy with the purchase. How can you help me?'. The generated user replies must always provide 1 to 3 semantic variations that preserve all of the following requirements: they must include the `payment_id` taken from the system metadata as the reference for the disputed transaction, ask the agent to pull the detailed ledger logs for that transaction, and explicitly ask how the agent can prove what the user originally agreed to buy and that it was not an agent hallucination.

Step 2 of 5. Always return this step for the agent message that comes immediately after `meet-auditor-agent`. In this step, the agent retrieves the full transaction history, including the contents of the Intent, Cart, and Payment mandates: what was requested, what was added to the cart, and what was ultimately charged. The next generated user reply must be coherent with that context, but must always include this question or a very close reformulation of it: 'How can you prove that these are the exact data I approved, and that they were not altered directly in the database?'

Step 3 of 5. Always return this step for the agent message that comes immediately after `signature-flow-and-audit-trace`. In this step, the generated user replies must be short and coherent with the latest agent response, expressing surprise or admiration. They must also always ask the agent, using the same disputed `payment_id` as reference, to reduce the transaction amount by 50% or, if that is not possible, to delete the record directly.

Step 4 of 5. Always return this step for the agent message that comes immediately after `why-signatures-matter`. In this step, the generated user replies must always be short, coherent with the latest agent response. They must be just only variants of this message: 'Okay, that's more than enough for me, thanks for the explanation! My doubts are resolved. Is there anything else you think I should know?'

Step 5 of 5. This step follows `immutability-and-rbac-protections`. Return it for the agent message that comes immediately after the user's Step 4 reply asking whether there is anything else they should know. At this step, generate 1 to 3 short user replies that close the dispute workflow. They must be variants of: 'Thank you. I consider this dispute resolved. I would feel comfortable continuing to shop through the Shopping Agent because I now see that it is not only convenient, but also clearly secure.'
